verdict.rationale: Otter documents its own "speaker recognition" in live transcription and lists "taggable speakers" on its pricing page, so it can attribute transcript text to speakers that users can label with names. However, the evidence is only two brief marketing lines: it does not show whether real names are matched automatically or only tagged by hand, and nothing in the pack speaks to attribution accuracy. missing for 10: documentation of automatic real-name matching to participants (e.g., via calendar or voice profiles), detail on diarization quality and how tags carry across meetings, independent or hands-on corroboration of correct speaker attribution.

support.subject: As a product manager, the transcript attributes words to the right named speakers (diarization plus real name matching), not just "Speaker 1/2"

citations.quote: Live transcription in multiple languages, and speaker recognition.
